text.p: Here are the highlights of stories in the Danish press on Wednesday. Reuters has not verified these stories and does not vouch for their accuracy.
--- A new survey from Denmark's confederation of Industry says that 40 percent of companies expect to have more employees abroad in five years.

--- The limit for tv-commercials' share of the entire advertising market seems to have been reached as the TV-commercial share of the total advertising turnover ended at 31.8 percent in 1995 compared to 1994 where TV-commercials had 30.7 percent of the entire advertising market.

--- The police are to start permanent surveillance of biker group Hells Angels' two locations in Copenhagen to increase security for locals in the area. At the same time minister of justice Bjoern Westh is to intensify surveillance of biker locations in the rest of Denmark.

--- The President of Lithuania Algirdis Brazauskas and his daughter are to visit Denmark from October 9 to 11. Brazauskas and his daughter are to stay with the queen during their visit and meet with a number of Danish politicians.

--- Denmark's largest privately owned animal feed company KFK is to become the largest in Scandinavia with its takeover of Sweden's second largest feed company Svenska Foder with a turnover of 1.3 billion Swedish crowns in 1995.

--- Minister of justice Bjoern Westh says that Denmark is to increase pressure on Sweden to get better rules for compensation in the event of an accident at the Swedish nuclear plant of Barsebaek in the south of Sweden close to Copenhagen.
